# Reporting Issues

This codebase is worked on primarily by AI agents. This guide is for
them.

**The more technical detail, the better.** File paths with line numbers,
exact symbols, transcript IDs, commit SHAs, error output verbatim,
stack traces, environment variables — over-share rather than
under-share. Every fact you omit is a follow-up round trip the next
person has to do before they can reproduce.

## Which repo

| Repo | What goes here |
|---|---|
| **agent-code** | UI, tile-tree, dispatch, session management, IPC, system-perf, settings — all renderer + main-process behaviour. Default. |
| **claude-code-headless** | Driving the real `claude` CLI: TUI parsing, JSONL handling, proxy/SSE streaming, slash-picker, permission prompts. |
| **codex-headless** | Driving the real `codex` CLI: rollout parsing, Responses adapter, screen parsing, approval overlays. |
| **agent-transcript-parser** | Claude↔Codex transcript translation, ghost primitives, rewind/clone helpers. |
| **agent-voice-dictation** | Recording, STT clients, OpenRouter polish, composer integration. |

## Bug report

```markdown
### What happened
One or two sentences. The visible symptom.

### Repro
Exact steps. If non-deterministic, say so explicitly and describe how
often / under what conditions: "happens after ~30 min of normal use
with 10+ agents active." Link the relevant transcript path —
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-foo-bar/<sessionId>.jsonl` for Claude or
`~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-<timestamp>-<id>.jsonl` for
Codex. Include the commit SHA you reproduced on.

### Where
File:line and the function or symbol if you've located it. Examples:
`src/main/sessionManager.ts:912 spawnClaude`,
`src/renderer/src/features/feed/ui/Feed.tsx onScroll`,
`packages/claude-code-headless/src/proxy/ClaudeProxyAdapter.ts:804`.
If unlocated, name the subsystem: feed renderer, JSONL tailer, proxy
adapter, dispatch mode, work-context, image paste, dictation.

### Output
Error text, stack trace, log lines — verbatim, don't paraphrase or
truncate. Include surrounding console lines if a single line was the
trigger but the context is in the lines around it. Native frames
(C++/Rust) in a v8 fatal-error trace are important — keep them.

### State
Anything that affects reproducibility: number of active panes, which
providers (Claude / Codex / terminal), how long the app had been
running, whether `AGENT_CODE_PERF` was set, whether you were in
Dispatch Mode, whether worktrees were attached.
```

## Feature request

```markdown
### Use case
The workflow the current app makes harder than it should be.

### Example
One concrete scenario, end to end — what you'd do today vs. what you
wish you could do.

### (Optional) Sketch
Implementation thoughts. Skip unless you have specifics.
```

## Performance / crash

Different evidence than functional bugs. Attach what applies:

- **Fatal-error block from the terminal.** When the main process
  OOM's, the terminal where `npm start` ran will have a `FATAL
  ERROR: CALL_AND_RETRY_LAST Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out
  of memory` line followed by a `Native stack trace` block. Include
  the whole block, not just the headline — the native frames identify
  the allocator that broke (typical signatures: `node::Buffer::New`,
  `v8::CppHeap::wrapper_descriptor`, Rust `font_types::...`).
- **System-perf popover state at the time.** Requires
  `AGENT_CODE_PERF=1` set when launching. Click the heap badge in the
  header. Report: heap used / limit, RSS, top heap spaces with sizes
  (especially `old_space` and `large_object_space`),
  detached-contexts count, native-contexts count, event-loop p99,
  60s growth Δ for heap and RSS.
- **Heap snapshot.** Manual: click "Capture heap snapshot" in the
  popover; writes to `~/.config/agent-code/heap-snapshots/manual-<iso>-<pid>.heapsnapshot`.
  Automatic: the watchdog writes one when `used_heap_size` crosses
  `min(3 GiB, 0.75 × heap_size_limit)` — same directory, `main-` prefix.
  These files are 10–500 MB; link a cloud share rather than attaching
  directly if large.
- **Growth pattern.** Three shapes matter:
  - steady monotonic climb → retention leak
  - spike-up-then-drop-to-zero cycle → transient large allocations
    (whole-file reads, big buffers, GC churn)
  - sudden jump → one-shot allocation (giant string, image, file load)

  Saying which shape you observed narrows the suspect list before
  anyone opens the snapshot.

## Security

Disclose privately to the maintainer rather than via a public GitHub
issue.

## Don't file

- How-to questions → Discussions.
- Upstream CLI bugs (`claude` / `codex` flag behaviour) → the upstream
  repos for those tools, not here.

I've now read through the project's core documentation, structure, and history. Here's the complete picture of what **Agent Code** is.

---

# Agent Code — what this project is

**Agent Code is an open-source, Electron-based, AI-native IDE** — an "agent-first editor" built for people who run Claude Code and Codex *all day, in parallel*. It's written and maintained almost entirely by AI agents (you), with the repo itself being the only shared memory between sessions.

It's your own project (juliusolsson.com/agent-code), currently at version `0.0.2-beta.1`.

## The core thesis

Most people building Claude Code UIs make one of two mistakes:
1. They optimize for **looks** instead of agent capability ("Claude Code but prettier").
2. They **bypass the real product** — driving the limited SDK or reusing OAuth tokens against private/reduced interfaces, which throws away ~75% of the functionality that lives in the real CLIs.

Agent Code takes the opposite stance: **the agent runtime is the product; the UI exists to make it more powerful.** It runs the *full, real* `claude` and `codex` CLIs headlessly inside PTYs — not the stripped-down SDK — so the entire command surface, prompts, tools, permission flows, and runtime behavior are preserved. Claude Code should still feel like Claude Code; Codex should still feel like Codex. If it ends up looking nicer, that's incidental — capability comes first.

## The strategic bet (from MANIFESTO.md)

The motivating insight: **OAuth is being killed.** You can no longer use Anthropic models properly in OpenCode, and Cursor's pricing punishes you for using SOTA external models. The prediction is that the "open API" era of AI tools will close fast (history rhyming with how Facebook/Google/Yahoo killed their open APIs in the 2010s, but compressed into ~5 years). So instead of going *around* Claude Code and Codex, Agent Code becomes **the middleman** that drives them natively.

## How it works architecturally

A headless CLI for Claude/Codex is spawned in a PTY and controlled programmatically. The stack combines terminal emulation, JSON/event parsing, screen parsing, transcript parsing, and session management — exposing the real CLIs in an API-like way. On top sits an **Electron + React workspace shell**.

It's deliberately split into **separately-scoped packages** (in `packages/`) — partly so each can attract its own open-source contributors:

| Package | Role |
|---|---|
| **claude-code-headless** | Drives the real `claude` CLI — TUI parsing, JSONL handling, proxy/SSE streaming, slash-picker, permission prompts |
| **codex-headless** | Drives the real `codex` CLI — rollout parsing, Responses adapter, screen parsing, approval overlays |
| **opencode-headless** | (additional headless control layer) |
| **agent-transcript-parser** | Translates JSONL transcripts between Claude ↔ Codex with roundtrip safety — this is what powers **one-click provider switching** mid-session |
| **agent-voice-dictation** | Open-source WhisprFlow clone on Deepgram; ships voice dictation natively into the composer (wraps STT output in an `<stt>` tag so the *model* fixes transcription errors, not a dumb pre-pass) |

## The four differentiators

1. **Provider switching** — open a Codex session, hit the command palette, switch to Claude in one click via native transcript translation.
2. **Heavy-development focus** — the real CLIs feel built for *one* session on screen; serious use means 5+ agents running at once. Agent Code gives you tiling/grid layout to manage them.
3. **Custom rendering** — as the middleman, all rendering is rewritten in React (e.g. a better UI for what agents committed and which git commands they ran).
4. **Opinionated for efficiency** — all terminals and agents are **tmux-persistent by default**; 50+ productivity commands layered on top.

## Source layout (`src/`)

- **`src/main/`** — Electron main process: `sessions`, `orchestration` (multi-agent), `aiWorkspace`, `tmux`, `providerSwitch`, `dictation`, `caffeinate`, `worktreeActivity`, `performance`, `storage`, `ipc`
- **`src/renderer/`** — React workspace UI (feed, tiling, panes)
- **`src/providers/`** — `claude`, `codex`, `shared` adapters
- **`src/mcp/`** — MCP runtime support
- **`src/shared/`** — git, parsers, runtime, types, work-context, rendered-content

## Repo conventions worth knowing

- **`vendor/`** = read-only source references (`claude-code-src`, `codex-src`) for grepping upstream implementations — never built or shipped.
- **`third_party/`** = pinned *runtime artifacts* the packaged app ships (`mitmproxy`, `tmux`); binaries are never committed — a `manifest.json` (version + per-arch sha256 + URL) is the source of truth.
- **Thick WHY comments** are mandated — explain *why* code exists and what would make it wrong, not what it does. Decision-making lives in the diff, not in drifting docs.
- **Issues** are written by AI agents for AI agents — maximal technical detail (file:line, transcript paths, commit SHAs, verbatim errors).
- Testing recently moved to **Vitest** (commit #263), with unit / integration / renderer projects.

## Current state

Active build. Already working: Claude Code sessions, Codex sessions, plain terminals, tabbed + tiled workspace UI, provider-aware session handling, transcript/runtime parsing, and local desktop hosting via Electron. Recent commit activity is heavily focused on the **feed rendering rewrite** and **orchestration** (multi-agent context inheritance, handoff scanning) — there are active rewrite plans in `docs/rendering/` and `docs/codex-rewrite-render/`.

---

In one line: **Agent Code is an Electron IDE that wraps the *real* Claude Code and Codex CLIs (not their reduced SDKs) to give power users parallel, tiled, persistent, provider-switchable agent sessions — betting that owning the middleman layer is the durable position as OAuth/open-API access gets locked down.**

Want me to go deeper on any specific subsystem — the orchestration/multi-agent layer, the rendering rewrite that's currently in flight, or how provider switching actually works under the hood?

# Tiled Dispatch

## Summary

Add a `Tiled Dispatch` command that lets the user enter a tile count, up to 10, and opens a multi-lane Dispatch layout where several live agents can be viewed and controlled at the same time.

## Problem

Dispatch Mode is useful for managing many agents, but it currently behaves like a single command-center surface. That means the user can see the list of agents, pick one, and work with that agent, but they cannot easily keep multiple active agents visible side by side from the Dispatch workflow.

When coordinating several Claude/Codex agents, the user often wants both:

- A full Dispatch index with all worktrees, section titles, agent types, and full agent titles.
- Multiple live agent views on screen at once, each with a small local selector for switching that lane to another agent.

The existing single Dispatch surface makes that workflow too serial.

## Proposed Behavior

Add a command:

```text
Tiled Dispatch
```

When run, the command prompts the user for a number:

```text
How many dispatch tiles? 1-10
```

After the user enters `N`, Agent Code enters a tiled Dispatch layout:

```text
┌──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┬────────────┬──────────────────────────────┬────────────┬──────────────────────────────┐
│ DISPATCH INDEX       │ AGENT VIEW 1                 │ MINI LIST  │ AGENT VIEW 2                 │ MINI LIST  │ AGENT VIEW 3                 │

```

For `N` tiled lanes, the conceptual layout is:

```text
[full dispatch index] [agent view 1] [mini list 2] [agent view 2] ... [mini list N] [agent view N]
```

The first lane is special:

- It keeps the full Dispatch list UI.
- It shows full section titles.
- It shows worktree/project grouping.
- It shows agent type/provider labels.
- It acts as the global index for the whole tiled Dispatch layout.

Every later lane uses a compact local selector:

- It shows a minimal agent list.
- It omits repeated section titles.
- It omits repeated worktree labels.
- It omits repeated agent type/provider labels.
- It is only there to switch which agent is shown in that lane.

Each lane still has a real live agent view beside its list. This is not just multiple copies of the Dispatch list; the point is to make multiple agents visible and usable at the same time.

## Scroll and Selection Sync

When the user scrolls a compact mini list, the full Dispatch index on the far left should follow that scroll position enough to keep the same region of the agent list/context visible. The full index remains the source of truth for rich context: section titles, worktrees, provider labels, and full agent titles.

Selection highlighting is separate from scroll sync:

- The full index still highlights the agent selected in lane 1.
- A compact mini list highlights the agent selected for its own lane.
- Scrolling mini list 3 should move the full index to the same approximate list region, but it should not make the full index pretend that lane 3's agent is selected.
- This lets the user use the full left index as context while still seeing exactly which agent belongs to lane 1.

In other words:

```text
Lane 3 mini list scrolls
        │
        ▼
Full left index follows scroll/context
        │
        └── but selected highlight remains Agent 1 / lane 1
```

## UX Notes

- The default tile count should be conservative, probably `2` or the previous value if one exists.
- The max should be clamped to `10`.
- The layout needs horizontal overflow or responsive compression for high tile counts.
- The first/full Dispatch index should stay readable even when there are many lanes.
- Compact mini lists should be dense and stable, optimized for quick lane switching.
- The selected agent per lane should be independent.
- Switching one lane should not steal focus or selection from the other lanes.
- Scrolling a compact mini list should sync the full index's scroll context, while preserving the full index's own selected-agent highlight.

## Open Questions

- Should tiled Dispatch persist across app reloads, or should it be a transient Dispatch view mode?
- Should each lane remember its selected agent by session id across normal Dispatch exits/reentries?
- Should lane widths be resizable?
- Should the full index lane be pinned/sticky while the right-side lanes horizontally scroll?
- Should tile count changes preserve current lane selections where possible?

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `Tiled Dispatch` command exists.
- Running it prompts for a tile count from `1` to `10`.
- Entering a valid count opens a tiled Dispatch layout.
- The leftmost lane shows the full Dispatch index with section titles, worktree grouping, provider/agent type labels, and full titles.
- Each additional lane shows a compact mini list plus the actual selected agent view to its right.
- Each lane can select a different live agent.
- Scrolling a compact mini list scroll-syncs the full left Dispatch index to the same general list region.
- The full left Dispatch index continues to highlight lane 1's selected agent, even while its scroll position follows another lane's mini list.
- The same agent process/session is reused; switching tiled views must not respawn agents.
- Exiting tiled Dispatch returns the user to the normal workspace without killing agents.
- Invalid counts are rejected or clamped safely.

That's **issue #248 — "Tiled Dispatch"** (no labels, no comments yet). Here's what it's about.

## The problem it solves
Dispatch Mode today is a **single command-center surface**: you see the list of all your agents, pick *one*, and work with it. That's serial. When you're coordinating 5+ Claude/Codex agents, you want two things at once that the current design can't give you:

1. A **full index** of every agent (worktrees, section titles, provider labels, full titles).
2. **Several live agent views side-by-side**, each independently switchable.

## The proposed feature
A new command, **`Tiled Dispatch`**, that prompts: *"How many dispatch tiles? 1–10"*. Enter `N` and you get a multi-lane layout:

```
[full dispatch index] [agent view 1] [mini list 2] [agent view 2] … [mini list N] [agent view N]
```

- **Lane 1 is special** — it keeps the *full* Dispatch list: section titles, worktree/project grouping, provider/type labels. It's the global index for the whole layout.
- **Every later lane** gets a **compact mini-list** (no repeated section titles/worktrees/labels — just enough to switch that lane) plus its own **live agent view** beside it.
- Each lane shows a *different live agent*, and they're independent — switching one lane doesn't steal focus or selection from another.

## The clever bit — scroll vs. selection decoupling
This is the subtle design point. When you scroll a mini-list (say lane 3), the **full left index follows that scroll position** so you keep rich context for the region you're browsing — **but the left index's *highlight* stays on lane 1's selected agent.** So scrolling lane 3 moves the index's viewport without making it pretend lane 3's agent is "selected." Scroll-sync and selection-highlight are deliberately separate concerns.

## Key constraints (acceptance criteria worth flagging)
- Count clamped to **1–10**; default conservative (2).
- **Same agent process/session is reused** — switching tiled views must *not respawn* agents.
- **Exiting tiled Dispatch must not kill agents** — returns to normal workspace.
- Needs horizontal overflow / responsive compression for high tile counts.

## Open questions still unresolved
- Persist across app reloads, or transient view mode?
- Should each lane remember its agent by session id across exits?
- Resizable lane widths? Pinned/sticky full-index lane while right lanes scroll horizontally?
- Preserve lane selections when tile count changes?

In short: it turns Dispatch from a one-agent-at-a-time command center into a **tiled, multi-lane cockpit** — one rich master index on the left, plus N independently-controllable live agent panes, with scroll-context sync that doesn't clobber per-lane selection. It directly serves the project's "run 5+ agents at once" thesis.

Note: this is the only issue about viewing multiple Dispatch lanes at once. (#236 and #261 are related Dispatch *bugs* — focus-stealing and focus-on-close — but #248 is the multi-lane feature itself.)

Every project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. "Simple" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. ### (a) TILE-TREE TYPES & STORE

**Type Definitions** (`/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/types.ts`):

- **Lines 23-42**: Core TileNode recursive union type:
  ```
  type TileNode = 
    | { type: 'leaf'; sessionId: SessionId }
    | { type: 'split'; direction: 'vertical' | 'horizontal'; 
        ratio: number; a: TileNode; b: TileNode }
  ```
  - Binary splits only (no arbitrary N-way splits)
  - `a` = left/top side, `b` = right/bottom side
  - `ratio` = fraction of space given to `a` (clamped 0.1–0.9)
  - Vertical split = side-by-side (divider runs top-to-bottom)
  - Horizontal split = stacked (divider runs left-to-right)

- **Lines 44-49**: Tab structure:
  ```

    id: TabId
    title: string
    root: TileNode        // The tile tree for this tab
    focusedSessionId: SessionId  // Which pane has focus in this tab

  ```

  - `tabs: Tab[]` - array of tabs, each with its own tile tree
  - `activeTabId` - which tab is currently visible
  - `sessions: Record<SessionId, SessionMeta>` - metadata for all live sessions
  - `detachedSessions` - sessions not in any tile tree (Dispatch Mode only)
  - `buried` - hidden-but-live sessions removed from layout
  - `dispatchMode: DispatchModeState | null` - Dispatch Mode state (mutually exclusive with grid)

- **Lines 62-88** of `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/hook/index.ts` show zustand slices:

### (e) FOCUS MODEL

**Grid Focus**:
- `Tab.focusedSessionId: SessionId` — which pane in this tab is active
- Updated by `focusSession(id)` (lines 1452-1467) or `focusSessionInTab(tabId, id)` (lines 1469-1490)
- Used to:
  - Highlight the pane's border (CSS class in TileLeaf based on `focused` prop)
  - Auto-focus input field in that pane
  - Determine which pane receives keybinds (composer, navigation, split commands)
  - Determine which split to resize on ← → ↑ ↓ keybinds
- Single focus per tab; only one pane can be focused at a time

**Dispatch Focus** (separate from grid):
- `dispatchMode.focusedSessionId: SessionId | undefined` — which row in dispatch list is highlighted
- Lives on `DispatchModeState`, NOT `Tab.focusedSessionId`
- Reason: Tab.focusedSessionId is "grid-only" invariant (lines 848-851 of pane.ts)
- Dispatch rows are session selections in a picker, not leaf panes
- When exiting Dispatch, grid focus is untouched (preserved by separate field)

- Grid: Dispatch geometric neighbor lookup via `findBestRemainingFocus(previousRoot, nextRoot, removedSessionId)` (geometry.ts, lines 200-222)
  - Finds closest remaining pane to the removed one's center
  - Falls back to surviving sibling leaf
- Dispatch: row-by-index successor (keeps visual position like native list pickers)

**Focus stealing issues** (#261, #236):
- Multiple subsystems can request focus (pane click, type-to-focus, paste-to-focus, spotlight click, etc.)
- All converge on `focusSession(id)` call

**Multi-Tab Architecture**:
- `WorkspaceState.tabs: Tab[]` — array of independent workspaces
- `WorkspaceState.activeTabId` — which tab is currently displayed
- Each Tab has its own `TileNode root` tree and `focusedSessionId`
- Tabs are NOT sub-grids within a larger grid; they are top-level workspaces
- Each tab has independent session list (though sessions live in global `WorkspaceState.sessions`)
- Closing a tab does NOT kill its sessions (they continue running, become orphaned, or are revived)

type TileTabsState = {
  tabIds: TabId[]
  focusedTabId: TabId
  direction: SplitDirection
  ratios: number[]

```
- **Mutually exclusive with DispatchMode** (layoutCommands.ts line 8 comment)
- Shows multiple tabs side-by-side in a tiled layout
- Tabs themselves are not recursively split; they form a top-level linear sequence
- Direction = 'vertical' (tabs side-by-side columns) or 'horizontal' (stacked rows)
- Ratios array = sizes for each tab
- `focusedTabId` = which tab (not which pane within a tab) is focused

- Dispatch mode: 1 visible grid tab + 1 visible dispatch list + optional project terminal (mutually exclusive with grid)

**REUSE POTENTIAL: HIGH with CAVEATS**

**What IS reusable**:

1. **Pure tree operations** (treeOps.ts):
   - `splitLeaf`, `closeLeaf`, `wrapRootWithNode`, `normalizeTree`, `rotateTree` are 100% decoupled
   - Could build a second TileNode tree for Dispatch layout without touching these
   - `collectLeaves`, `remapTileTreeSessionIds` also work on any TileNode

2. **Geometry functions** (geometry.ts):
   - `buildLeafGeometries`, `findDirectionalNeighbor`, `findBestRemainingFocus` work on any TileNode
   - Pure functions, no store coupling
   - Could drive navigation in a Dispatch Tiled view

3. **Divider resize logic** (TileTree.tsx SplitContainer, lines 167-211):
   - Mouse-down handler, `requestAnimationFrame` batching, epsilon logic are portable
   - Only coupling is `workspace.setSplitRatioInTab(tabId, aSessionId, bSessionId, nextRatio)` call
   - Could be extracted to a reusable hook or abstracted away

4. **Session rendering pipeline**:
   - `renderWorkspaceLeaf`, `getRendererProvider(kind)` dispatch pattern is decoupled
   - Leaf components (TileLeaf, TerminalLeaf) are already composable via provider pattern
   - Could reuse same TileLeaf / TerminalLeaf rendering inside Dispatch tiles

**What BREAKS reuse / requires coupling**:

1. **Store integration**:
   - Currently, TileNode lives inside `WorkspaceState.tabs[].root`
   - If Dispatch has its own tile tree, needs separate `dispatchTileTree: TileNode | null` field on WorkspaceState
   - Tree mutations would need separate action set: `splitDispatchTile`, `closeDispatchTile`, `resizeDispatchTile`, etc.
   - **ALTERNATIVE**: Dispatch could nest inside a pseudo-Tab (a synthetic Tab-like object not in the tabs array), but that's coupling too

   - Grid uses `Tab.focusedSessionId`
   - Dispatch already uses `DispatchModeState.focusedSessionId` (a different field!)
   - **If Tiled Dispatch exists**: which focus field owns it?
     - If `DispatchModeState.focusedSessionId`, then navigation/keybinds must know "which surface am I on?"
     - If a new `dispatchTileTree` field, needs its own focus id

3. **Persistence**:
   - PersistedWorkspace.tabs is TileNode array (one per tab)
   - Tiled Dispatch state would need to be added: `persistedWorkspace.dispatchTileTree?: TileNode | null`
   - Rehydration already handles TileNode remapping; could reuse that on Dispatch tree

4. **Rendering context**:
   - TileTree.tsx recursively renders any TileNode
   - Dispatch currently uses DispatchLayout.tsx (completely separate component)
   - Dispatch rendering is fundamentally different: list UI + detached sessions, not a tile grid
   - **Could reuse TileTree for rendering IF** Dispatch Tiled mode stops being a command-center list and becomes a true grid (breaking change)

5. **Coupling through workspace actions**:
   - All tile mutations (split, close, resize) go through pane.ts actions
   - If Dispatch had its own tree, need parallel dispatch.ts actions or a generic `splitInTree(treeType, ...)` abstraction
   - Keybind routing would need surface-awareness

6. **Session lifecycle**:
   - Grid-placed sessions live in `tab.root`, detached sessions live in `detachedSessions`
   - Tiled Dispatch would need to decide: are tile leaves grid sessions or detached sessions?
   - If grid: closing a pane closes a grid leaf (moves from tab.root to buried)
   - If detached: keep them detached even if they're in a tile layout (coupling with Dispatch semantics)

**VERDICT**: 

Tiled Dispatch CAN reuse 70% of tile infrastructure (tree ops, geometry, rendering dispatch, divider dragging) **IF** designed as:
- A separate `dispatchTileTree: TileNode | null` field on WorkspaceState
- Parallel action set (splitDispatchTile, closeDispatchTile, etc.)
- Shared focus field (`dispatchMode.focusedSessionId`) already exists for navigation
- Detached sessions continue living in `detachedSessions` (not tile leaves)
- Reuse `renderWorkspaceLeaf` + provider pattern for rendering leaves
- Reuse pure tree ops (treeOps.ts) and geometry (geometry.ts) without modification

**BREAKAGE RISK**: If you try to make Dispatch use the SAME Tab.root tree structure (like a grid tab), you'll hit session lifecycle conflicts (grid sessions vs. detached sessions are semantically different).

**SIMPLER APPROACH**: Make Dispatch Tiled a visual layout mode for the detached sessions list (rearrange their rendering into a split grid), without touching the TileNode data model at all. That avoids persistence, lifecycle, and focus coupling entirely.

I've now confirmed the load-bearing facts directly in the code. Here's what the exploration established and the design decision I want your sign-off on before I write the spec + plan.

## What the code tells us

**The good news — the session layer already supports this.** Swapping which agent a lane shows is *exactly* what `DispatchLayout` already does today with its single `activeRow`: it calls `renderWorkspaceLeaf(sessionId, …)` (line 187), and changing that `sessionId` does **not** kill the previously-shown agent. Sessions are killed only by an explicit `closeSession` action, never on unmount. Input, output subscriptions, and runtime are all keyed by `sessionId` globally — not per-view. So "N lanes, each showing a different live agent, switchable, no respawn, no kill on exit" needs **zero changes to the session manager**, as long as we hold one constraint (below).

**The one hazard, and how we dodge it:** the only thing that assumes 1:1 view↔session is the *terminal* xterm attach (a `Set`, single attacher) and replay buffers. Agents (Claude/Codex feeds) are fine to mount many times. So the rule that keeps us out of a session-manager refactor: **a given session can occupy at most one lane at a time** — the mini-lists grey out any agent already shown in another lane. That's also better UX (no reason to mirror one agent into two lanes) and it makes the whole feature additive.

**The layout should NOT be a tile-tree.** The issue spec is a *flat horizontal sequence of lanes*, never a recursive split. Reusing the `TileNode` tree would drag in persistence/lifecycle/focus coupling for no benefit. The clean shape is a **lane array** living inside the existing `dispatchMode` state, rendered with the resizer primitives that are already there (`useResizableSplitter` + `SplitHandle`, line 97/177).

## Recommended architecture

- Extend `DispatchModeState` (`types.ts:237`) with an optional `tiled?: { lanes: DispatchLane[] }`, where `DispatchLane = { selectedSessionId?: SessionId; scrollAnchorKey?: string }`. Lane 0 is the full index (reuses today's `DispatchAgentList`); lanes 1..N-1 get a compact mini-list + their own agent view.
- `DispatchLayout` forks at the top: `tiled` present → new `TiledDispatchLayout` component; absent → today's classic single-agent layout, untouched.
- Each lane's agent view is just another `renderWorkspaceLeaf(lane.selectedSessionId, …)` call — same code path, N times.
- New command `Tiled Dispatch` (added to `layoutCommands.ts`) prompts for a count 1–10, builds the lane array, enters dispatch mode tiled.
- Keybinds (`useKeybinds.ts`) become lane-aware: the focused *lane* owns arrow/cmd-N selection; the existing flat-row logic gets a "which lane" parameter.

This touches ~5 files, adds one component + one selector module, and leaves the grid, tile-tree, and session manager alone.

## The 5 open questions — my recommended answers (please confirm or override)

1. **Persist tiled view across reloads?** → **Yes, persist** the lane array (it already lives in `dispatchMode`, which is persisted). Cheap, and matches how everything else in dispatch survives restart.
2. **Each lane remembers its agent by session id across exit/re-entry?** → **Yes** — store `selectedSessionId` per lane; on re-entry, drop any lane whose session no longer exists and fall back to the next visible agent.
3. **Resizable lane widths?** → **Yes**, reuse `useResizableSplitter` per boundary, store a `ratios` array. (Low cost, the primitive exists.)
4. **Sticky/pinned full index while right lanes horizontally scroll?** → **Yes** — lane 0 (full index) is fixed-width and pinned; the lane strip to its right is what overflows/scrolls horizontally at high tile counts.
5. **Preserve lane selections when the count changes?** → **Yes** — growing keeps existing lanes and appends; shrinking drops from the right. Never respawns or reshuffles.

My one **YAGNI trim** vs. the issue: I'd **defer the scroll-sync feature** (scrolling a mini-list nudges the full index to the same region while keeping lane 0's highlight) to a follow-up. It's the fiddliest part (two-way scroll coupling that must not move selection) and it's pure polish — the core "see and drive N agents at once" value lands without it. I'd build the lanes first, add scroll-sync as a phase 2 if you still want it.

Does this architecture + the 5 answers + deferring scroll-sync look right? Once you confirm, I'll write the design spec to `docs/superpowers/specs/` and then the implementation plan.

# Tiled Dispatch

## Summary

Add a `Tiled Dispatch` command that lets the user enter a tile count, up to 10, and opens a multi-lane Dispatch layout where several live agents can be viewed and controlled at the same time.

## Problem

Dispatch Mode is useful for managing many agents, but it currently behaves like a single command-center surface. That means the user can see the list of agents, pick one, and work with that agent, but they cannot easily keep multiple active agents visible side by side from the Dispatch workflow.

When coordinating several Claude/Codex agents, the user often wants both:

- A full Dispatch index with all worktrees, section titles, agent types, and full agent titles.
- Multiple live agent views on screen at once, each with a small local selector for switching that lane to another agent.

The existing single Dispatch surface makes that workflow too serial.

## Proposed Behavior

Add a command:

```text
Tiled Dispatch
```

When run, the command prompts the user for a number:

```text
How many dispatch tiles? 1-10
```

After the user enters `N`, Agent Code enters a tiled Dispatch layout:

```text
┌──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┬────────────┬──────────────────────────────┬────────────┬──────────────────────────────┐
│ DISPATCH INDEX       │ AGENT VIEW 1                 │ MINI LIST  │ AGENT VIEW 2                 │ MINI LIST  │ AGENT VIEW 3                 │
│ full list            │ selected agent               │ compact    │ selected agent               │ compact    │ selected agent               │
│                      │                              │            │                              │            │                              │
│ Worktree: app        │ ┌──────────────────────────┐ │ ● Agent A  │ ┌──────────────────────────┐ │ ● Agent B  │ ┌──────────────────────────┐ │
│  Claude  Agent A  ◀  │ │ Claude/Codex transcript  │ │ ● Agent B◀ │ │ Claude/Codex transcript  │ │ ● Agent C◀ │ │ Claude/Codex transcript  │ │
│  Codex   Agent B     │ │ composer / terminal      │ │ ● Agent C  │ │ composer / terminal      │ │ ● Agent D  │ │ composer / terminal      │ │
│  Claude  Agent C     │ │ live output              │ │ ● Agent D  │ │ live output              │ │ ● Agent E  │ │ live output              │ │
│                      │ │                          │ │            │ │                          │ │            │ │                          │ │
│ Worktree: issue-211  │ │ selected from index      │ │ no groups  │ │ selected from mini list  │ │ no groups  │ │ selected from mini list  │ │
│  Codex   Agent D     │ └──────────────────────────┘ │ no cwd     │ └──────────────────────────┘ │ no cwd     │ └──────────────────────────┘ │
│  Claude  Agent E     │                              │ no type    │                              │ no type    │                              │
└──────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┴────────────┴──────────────────────────────┴────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘
```

For `N` tiled lanes, the conceptual layout is:

```text
[full dispatch index] [agent view 1] [mini list 2] [agent view 2] ... [mini list N] [agent view N]
```

The first lane is special:

- It keeps the full Dispatch list UI.
- It shows full section titles.
- It shows worktree/project grouping.
- It shows agent type/provider labels.
- It acts as the global index for the whole tiled Dispatch layout.

Every later lane uses a compact local selector:

- It shows a minimal agent list.
- It omits repeated section titles.
- It omits repeated worktree labels.
- It omits repeated agent type/provider labels.
- It is only there to switch which agent is shown in that lane.

Each lane still has a real live agent view beside its list. This is not just multiple copies of the Dispatch list; the point is to make multiple agents visible and usable at the same time.

## Scroll and Selection Sync

When the user scrolls a compact mini list, the full Dispatch index on the far left should follow that scroll position enough to keep the same region of the agent list/context visible. The full index remains the source of truth for rich context: section titles, worktrees, provider labels, and full agent titles.

Selection highlighting is separate from scroll sync:

- The full index still highlights the agent selected in lane 1.
- A compact mini list highlights the agent selected for its own lane.
- Scrolling mini list 3 should move the full index to the same approximate list region, but it should not make the full index pretend that lane 3's agent is selected.
- This lets the user use the full left index as context while still seeing exactly which agent belongs to lane 1.

In other words:

```text
Lane 3 mini list scrolls
        │
        ▼
Full left index follows scroll/context
        │
        └── but selected highlight remains Agent 1 / lane 1
```

## UX Notes

- The default tile count should be conservative, probably `2` or the previous value if one exists.
- The max should be clamped to `10`.
- The layout needs horizontal overflow or responsive compression for high tile counts.
- The first/full Dispatch index should stay readable even when there are many lanes.
- Compact mini lists should be dense and stable, optimized for quick lane switching.
- The selected agent per lane should be independent.
- Switching one lane should not steal focus or selection from the other lanes.
- Scrolling a compact mini list should sync the full index's scroll context, while preserving the full index's own selected-agent highlight.

## Open Questions

- Should tiled Dispatch persist across app reloads, or should it be a transient Dispatch view mode?
- Should each lane remember its selected agent by session id across normal Dispatch exits/reentries?
- Should lane widths be resizable?
- Should the full index lane be pinned/sticky while the right-side lanes horizontally scroll?
- Should tile count changes preserve current lane selections where possible?

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `Tiled Dispatch` command exists.
- Running it prompts for a tile count from `1` to `10`.
- Entering a valid count opens a tiled Dispatch layout.
- The leftmost lane shows the full Dispatch index with section titles, worktree grouping, provider/agent type labels, and full titles.
- Each additional lane shows a compact mini list plus the actual selected agent view to its right.
- Each lane can select a different live agent.
- Scrolling a compact mini list scroll-syncs the full left Dispatch index to the same general list region.
- The full left Dispatch index continues to highlight lane 1's selected agent, even while its scroll position follows another lane's mini list.
- The same agent process/session is reused; switching tiled views must not respawn agents.
- Exiting tiled Dispatch returns the user to the normal workspace without killing agents.
- Invalid counts are rejected or clamped safely.

That's **issue #248 — "Tiled Dispatch"** (no labels, no comments yet). Here's what it's about.

## The problem it solves
Dispatch Mode today is a **single command-center surface**: you see the list of all your agents, pick *one*, and work with it. That's serial. When you're coordinating 5+ Claude/Codex agents, you want two things at once that the current design can't give you:

1. A **full index** of every agent (worktrees, section titles, provider labels, full titles).
2. **Several live agent views side-by-side**, each independently switchable.

## The proposed feature
A new command, **`Tiled Dispatch`**, that prompts: *"How many dispatch tiles? 1–10"*. Enter `N` and you get a multi-lane layout:

```
[full dispatch index] [agent view 1] [mini list 2] [agent view 2] … [mini list N] [agent view N]
```

- **Lane 1 is special** — it keeps the *full* Dispatch list: section titles, worktree/project grouping, provider/type labels. It's the global index for the whole layout.
- **Every later lane** gets a **compact mini-list** (no repeated section titles/worktrees/labels — just enough to switch that lane) plus its own **live agent view** beside it.
- Each lane shows a *different live agent*, and they're independent — switching one lane doesn't steal focus or selection from another.

## The clever bit — scroll vs. selection decoupling
This is the subtle design point. When you scroll a mini-list (say lane 3), the **full left index follows that scroll position** so you keep rich context for the region you're browsing — **but the left index's *highlight* stays on lane 1's selected agent.** So scrolling lane 3 moves the index's viewport without making it pretend lane 3's agent is "selected." Scroll-sync and selection-highlight are deliberately separate concerns.

- Count clamped to **1–10**; default conservative (2).
- **Same agent process/session is reused** — switching tiled views must *not respawn* agents.
- **Exiting tiled Dispatch must not kill agents** — returns to normal workspace.
- Needs horizontal overflow / responsive compression for high tile counts.

- Persist across app reloads, or transient view mode?
- Should each lane remember its agent by session id across exits?
- Resizable lane widths? Pinned/sticky full-index lane while right lanes scroll horizontally?
- Preserve lane selections when tile count changes?

In short: it turns Dispatch from a one-agent-at-a-time command center into a **tiled, multi-lane cockpit** — one rich master index on the left, plus N independently-controllable live agent panes, with scroll-context sync that doesn't clobber per-lane selection. It directly serves the project's "run 5+ agents at once" thesis.

Note: this is the only issue about viewing multiple Dispatch lanes at once. (#236 and #261 are related Dispatch *bugs* — focus-stealing and focus-on-close — but #248 is the multi-lane feature itself.)

Excellent. Now I have enough information to write a thorough report. Let me compile all the findings:

---

## Dispatch Mode Architecture Map

I've conducted a thorough exploration of the Dispatch Mode implementation. Here's the complete architectural map:

### (a) ENTRY POINTS & COMMANDS

**Command Registration:**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/features/workspace/commands/layoutCommands.ts` (lines 6–27)
  - Command ID: `dispatch-mode`
  - Surface: `app` (visible in both grid and dispatch modes)
  - Title: "Dispatch Mode"
  - Triggers `ui.enterDispatchMode()` or `ui.exitDispatchMode()` via the toggle
  - Shows state label: "Off" / "Project" / "Global"

- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/features/workspace/commands/layoutCommands.ts` (lines 29–43)
  - Command ID: `global-dispatch`
  - Surface: `dispatch` (only visible when Dispatch Mode is on)
  - Calls `ui.enterGlobalDispatch()`

**Surface-Based Command Filtering:**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/features/command-palette/registry.ts` (lines 49–53)
  - `surfaceAvailable()` function gates commands:
    - `surface: 'grid'` → hidden when `dispatchModeEnabled`
    - `surface: 'dispatch'` → hidden when NOT `dispatchModeEnabled`
    - `surface: 'app'` / `'session'` / `'editor'` / `'debug'` → always visible

**What Running Dispatch Does:**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/hook/actions/dispatch.ts` (lines 111–132)
  - `enterDispatchMode()` sets `workspace.state.dispatchMode = { scope: 'project' | 'global', focusedSessionId?: SessionId }`
  - Calls `setTileTabs(null)` to hide TileTabsView
  - Does NOT automatically spawn terminal (that's now gated by `settings.dispatchProjectTerminal`)

---

### (b) UI COMPONENTS & RENDERING

**Main Dispatch Layout:**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchLayout.tsx`
  - Three-column layout (when terminal is visible):
    1. Agent list (left, resizable ratio-based width)
    2. Active agent pane (center, flex-1)
    3. Project terminal (right, 25% fixed width, only if `settings.dispatchProjectTerminal` = true)
  - Resizable list/pane split via `useResizableSplitter` hook
  - Ratio stored in `useAppStore(state => state.dispatchListRatio)` (clamped 0.15..0.5)

**Agent List Component (`DispatchAgentList`):**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchLayout.tsx` (lines 224–336)
  - Sticky header showing "Sessions" label + dispatch scope ("project" or "global")
  - Renders three row groups:
    1. **Pinned section** (if `pinnedRows.length > 0`) — always visible across scopes
    2. **Tab groups** (from `buildDispatchGroups()`) — each tab gets its own section header
    3. Within each group: grid rows, then detached rows, in order
  - Scroll behavior: `useLayoutEffect` scrolls the highlighted row into view without relying on `scrollIntoView()`
  - Active row highlighted with `data-dispatch-active="true"` attribute

**Row Component (`DispatchAgentListRow`):**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchLayout.tsx` (lines 365–482)
  - Renders as a button element
  - Index cell (left) shows activity color-coded (green=working, blue=running, orange=starting, red=exited, gray=idle)
  - Row contains:
    - Index label (e.g., "A1", "A2", or "★1" for pinned)
    - Session title (primary row) — uses cached latest user prompt for agents
    - Subtitle row: agent status text ("thinking", "working", "running", "idle", etc.) + worktree badge + agent-type badge ("Claude" / "Codex" / "Terminal")
    - Unread badge (NEW / ACTION) for output or attention-requiring states
    - Project chip (optional, pinned rows only): shows tab letter + tab title
  - Linked agents show at depth=1 with left-indent connector glyph "↳"

**Dispatch Empty State:**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchLayout.tsx` (lines 648–654)
  - Message: "no sessions in this dispatch scope"

**Active Agent Pane Rendering:**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchLayout.tsx` (lines 186–199)
  - Calls `renderWorkspaceLeaf(activeRow.sessionId, ...)` from TileTree
  - Same rendering logic as grid panes (TileLeaf or TerminalLeaf depending on `kind`)

---

### (c) DATA MODEL & STATE

**DispatchModeState (Workspace-Local):**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/types.ts` (lines 237–253)
  ```typescript
  type DispatchModeState = {
    scope: 'project' | 'global'
    focusedSessionId?: SessionId  // Mode-local selection, independent of grid focus
  }
  ```
- Lives in `WorkspaceState.dispatchMode` (persisted to disk via `workspace.json`)
- `null` when dispatch is off

**DispatchAgentRow (Derived Row Model):**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/dispatchSelectors.ts` (lines 6–21)
  ```typescript
  type DispatchAgentRow = {
    key: string                    // Unique React key
    label: string                  // "A1", "A2", "★1" (for cmd+N)
    globalIndex: number            // 1-based, run order across all visible rows
    tabId: TabId                   // Parent tab
    tabTitle: string
    tabIndex: number               // 0-based tab position
    sessionId: SessionId
    kind: SessionKind | undefined  // 'claude' | 'codex' | 'terminal'
    title: string                  // user-provided or derived from cwd basename
    placement: 'grid' | 'detached' // where the session lives
    depth: number                  // 0 (normal) | 1 (linked child)
  }
  ```

**Dispatch Tab Group (For Grouping):**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/dispatchSelectors.ts` (lines 23–27)
  ```typescript
  type DispatchTabGroup = {
    tab: Tab
    tabIndex: number
    rows: DispatchAgentRow[]
  }
  ```

**Row Building Functions:**
- **`buildDispatchGroups(state)`** — Main grouping logic
  - **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/dispatchSelectors.ts` (lines 29–143)
  - Filters tabs based on scope (project scope = active tab only; global = all tabs)
  - Collects grid leaves via `collectLeaves(tab.root)`
  - Collects detached sessions via `detachedDispatchSessionIdsForTab()`
  - Excludes pinned sessions from groups (rendered separately)
  - Processes nesting: linked agents and orchestration agents indent under parent
  - Returns `DispatchTabGroup[]` with rows in visual render order

- **`buildVisibleDispatchRows(state)`** — Complete visible row list
  - **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/dispatchSelectors.ts` (lines 149–162)
  - Concatenates: pinned rows + flattened groups
  - Single source of truth for "row N" semantics (keyboard nav, cmd+N, close-after-delete)

- **`buildPinnedDispatchRows(state)`** — Pinned section
  - **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/dispatchSelectors.ts` (lines 246–298)
  - Iterates `state.pinnedSessionIds` in order
  - Labels: `★1`, `★2`, etc.
  - Scope-aware: pinned rows appear in both project and global scope
  - Cross-project: includes project chip (tab letter + title) for disambiguation
  - Filters out terminals and non-existent sessions

- **`selectVisibleDispatchRow(rows, dispatchFocusedSessionId, gridFocusedSessionId)`**
  - **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/dispatchSelectors.ts` (lines 192–210)
  - Fallback resolution: tries dispatch focus first, then grid focus, then `rows[0]`
  - Handles stale/missing focus IDs gracefully

**Detached Sessions:**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/types.ts` (lines 214–235)
  ```typescript
  type DetachedSessionRecord = {
    sessionId: SessionId
    surface: 'dispatch'              // Only value currently (future-proofed)
    projectTabId: TabId              // Affinity for grouping, cwd, terminal selection
    projectTabTitle: string
    projectTabIndex: number
    detachedAt: number               // Timestamp for ordering
  }
  ```
- Stored in `WorkspaceState.detachedSessions`
- Sessions live in detached pool when user creates them in Dispatch or explicitly parks them

**Pinned Sessions:**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/types.ts` (lines 276–286)
- Stored as ordered array in `WorkspaceState.pinnedSessionIds`
- Filtered to exclude terminals
- First-pin-wins ordering (no reordering UI in v1)

**Session Ownership (Important for Understanding):**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/sessionOwnership.ts`
- Dispatch focus is **intentionally excluded** from ownership:
  - `collectOwnedSessionIds()` = grid leaves + detached + buried (metadata preservation)
  - `collectLiveProcessIds()` = grid leaves only (rehydrate spawning)
  - Detached/buried sessions are metadata-only; not spawned on restart until user acts on them

---

### (d) SELECTION → SURFACE FLOW

**Selection Handler (User Clicks Row):**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchLayout.tsx` (lines 397–399)
  - `DispatchAgentListRow` button onClick calls `focusSessionInTab(row.tabId, row.sessionId)`
  - Callback passed from parent

**Focus Action (Workspace State Update):**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/hook/actions/dispatch.ts` (lines 159–180)
  - `focusDispatchSession(tabId, sessionId)` updates:
    - `workspace.state.activeTabId = tabId`
    - `workspace.state.dispatchMode.focusedSessionId = sessionId`
  - Does NOT update `Tab.focusedSessionId` (that's tile-tree invariant, would break resize/spotlight)

**Sync Effect (Keep Workspace Aligned):**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchLayout.tsx` (lines 110–129)
  - useEffect watches `activeRow?.tabId` and `activeRow?.sessionId`
  - If workspace `activeTab` or `dispatchMode.focusedSessionId` differs, updates via `workspace.focusDispatchSession()`
  - Ensures global Dispatch with fallback rows keeps workspace focus aligned with visible row

**Rendering Effect (Active Pane):**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchLayout.tsx` (lines 186–199)
  - `activeRow` determines which agent renders in the center pane
  - Calls `renderWorkspaceLeaf(activeRow.sessionId, ...)` to mount TileLeaf or TerminalLeaf
  - If no `activeRow`, shows "no sessions in this dispatch scope" message

---

### (e) MODE ENTER/EXIT MECHANISM

**How Dispatch Becomes Active:**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/app/App.tsx` (lines 631–647)
  - Render condition: `activeTab && workspace.dispatchMode`
  - When true, mounts `<DispatchLayout />` instead of `<TileTree />`
  - Wraps in relative div for `NewAgentPlacementOverlay`

**Enter Dispatch:**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/hook/actions/dispatch.ts` (lines 111–132)
  - `enterDispatchMode(scope?: 'project' | 'global')`
  - Sets `dispatchMode: { scope, focusedSessionId: prev.dispatchMode?.focusedSessionId }`
  - Calls `setTileTabs(null)` to exit tiled-tabs view if active
  - Closes new-agent placement overlay
  - Does NOT spawn terminal (DispatchLayout's useEffect does if `settings.dispatchProjectTerminal`)

**Exit Dispatch:**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/hook/actions/dispatch.ts` (lines 134–139)
  - `exitDispatchMode()`
  - Sets `dispatchMode: null`
  - Returns to grid view (TileTree)
  - Leaves `focusedSessionId` on grid's active pane (never orphaned in impossible state)

**Switch Scope (Project ↔ Global):**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/hook/actions/dispatch.ts` (lines 141–157)
  - `setDispatchScope(scope)`
  - Updates `dispatchMode.scope` while keeping `focusedSessionId`
  - Re-filters rows but preserves selection if the row is still visible

**Terminal Spawning (Lazy):**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchLayout.tsx` (lines 131–141)
  - useEffect watches `terminalVisible` (from settings) and `activeTab.id`
  - Only calls `workspace.ensureDispatchTerminal()` if setting is ON
  - Prevents the "I turned it off but it came back" bug from old ephemeral `dispatchMode.terminalVisible`

---

### (f) FOCUS & KEYBOARD HANDLING

**Dispatch Focus (Selection State):**
- Stored in `workspace.state.dispatchMode?.focusedSessionId`
- Independent of grid focus (`Tab.focusedSessionId`)
- Used to highlight active row and determine which agent renders

**Keyboard Navigation:**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/tile-tree/useKeybinds.ts` (lines 476–505)
  - Arrow Up/Down: call `moveDispatchSelection(workspace, ±1)`
  - Vim keybinds (j/k): same
  - Only work when `workspace.dispatchMode` is active
  - Dispatch steals these before normal grid navigation

**Row Selection by Number (cmd-1..9):**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/tile-tree/useKeybinds.ts` (lines 424–445)
  - When `workspace.dispatchMode`:
    - Single digit (1–9): select Nth visible row directly
    - Two digits (e.g., cmd-1 then cmd-2): select row 12
    - Multi-digit support via `pendingDispatchDigit` and 500ms timeout
  - Global dispatch row labels: "A1", "A2", "B1", "B2", etc. (global index across all tabs)
  - Selection via `focusDispatchRowByIndex(workspace, index - 1)`

**Movement Helper:**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/tile-tree/useKeybinds.ts` (lines 727–753)
  - `moveDispatchSelection(workspace, delta)` wraps around at list edges
  - Uses `selectVisibleDispatchRow()` to resolve current position (handles stale focus)
  - Updates via `workspace.focusDispatchSession()`

**Scroll-Into-View (Highlight Follows):**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchLayout.tsx` (lines 241–266)
  - useLayoutEffect on `activeSessionId` change
  - Finds `[data-dispatch-active="true"]` row in DOM
  - Manually computes scroll based on list rect + header height
  - Prevents row from drifting outside viewport when navigating

**Command Target Resolution (Dispatch-Aware):**
- **File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/hook/selectors/commandTargetSessionId.ts`
  - `commandTargetSessionId(workspace)` returns `dispatchMode.focusedSessionId` when in dispatch
  - Falls back to `activeTab.focusedSessionId` in grid
  - Used by all destructive/selective commands (close, bury, pin, unpin, attach)

**Dispatch-Specific Commands Visible Only in Dispatch:**
- Pin Agents, Unpin Agent, Attach Detached Session
- Surface gate in registry prevents grid users from seeing them

---

### (g) ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRAINTS & SINGLETONS

**Single Agent Rendering Assumption:**
- **Location:** `DispatchLayout.tsx` always renders exactly ONE active agent pane (center column)
- Line 186–199: `{activeRow ? <TileLeaf /> : <empty>}`
- No multi-pane dispatch layout currently; the entire right 50–85% width is one `sessionId`

**Global Selected Agent (`activeRow`):**
- **Derived from:** `selectVisibleDispatchRow(rows, dispatchFocusedSessionId, gridFocusedSessionId)`
- Single `activeRow` object; all rendering depends on `activeRow.sessionId`
- If focus ID is stale, falls back to grid focus, then `rows[0]` (no "nothing selected" state)

**Terminal Ownership Per Tab:**
- **File:** `findTerminalSessionInTab()` returns at most ONE terminal per tab
- Dispatch renders the terminal in the right column if `terminalVisible && activeRow.sessionId !== terminalSessionId`
- Only grid-attached terminal or first detached terminal is shown; no terminal selection UI

**Hardcoded Three-Column Split:**
- **File:** `DispatchLayout.tsx` lines 150–221
  - List | (splitter) | Active Agent | Terminal
  - No configurable column count or tiling within dispatch
  - Terminal width is 25% fixed; list is ratio-based; agent absorbs rest via flex-1

**Resizable List/Agent Boundary Only:**
- **File:** `DispatchLayout.tsx` lines 80–108
  - Only the list/active-agent split is draggable via `useResizableSplitter`
  - Ratio stored globally in `useAppStore(state => state.dispatchListRatio)`
  - Clamped 0.15..0.5 to prevent list from becoming unreadable
  - Terminal is fixed 25%; not part of the splitter

**No Grid Hierarchy in Dispatch:**
- Sessions in dispatch are flat rows (or 1-level nested if linked/orchestration)
- No binary-split tree like in TileTree
- No focus-rect traversal or resize/collapse operations like grid panes

**Exclusive Surfaces (TileTree XOR DispatchLayout XOR TileTabsView):**
- **File:** `App.tsx` lines 631–668
  - `if (tileTabs)` → TileTabsView
  - `else if (dispatchMode)` → DispatchLayout
  - `else if (activeTab)` → TileTree
  - Mutually exclusive; can't render grid and dispatch simultaneously
  - Switching modes clears TileTabsView state (`setTileTabs(null)` on enter dispatch)

**No Dispatch in Tiled Tabs Mode:**
- TileTabsView is a separate layout mode (multiple tabs side-by-side)
- Entering dispatch must exit tiled-tabs first
- Two separate "layout modes" competing for the main view

---

### KEY FINDINGS FOR TILED DISPATCH DESIGN

**Hard Constraints (Would Block Multi-Lane Dispatch):**
1. **Single `activeRow` rendering** — DispatchLayout.tsx hard-codes one active agent pane
2. **Global focus state** — `dispatchMode.focusedSessionId` is a single ID, not a map
3. **List/Agent split singleton** — `dispatchListRatio` in app store is single value, not per-layout
4. **Fixed terminal width (25%)** — no config for terminal column size in multi-agent layout
5. **Exclusive mode rendering** — TileTree/DispatchLayout/TileTabsView can't coexist
6. **No binary-split tree in dispatch** — rows are flat or 1-level nested, no recursive layout

**Soft Constraints (Would Require Refactoring):**
- Row builders assume single scope (`project` or `global`), not per-pane
- `selectVisibleDispatchRow()` fallback logic assumes one "visible" row to highlight

## COMPREHENSIVE TILE-TREE SYSTEM ANALYSIS

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here is the complete map of the existing tiling/tile-tree workspace system:

---

### (a) TILE-TREE TYPES & STORE

**Type Definitions** (`/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/types.ts`):

- **Lines 23-42**: Core TileNode recursive union type:
  ```
  type TileNode = 
    | { type: 'leaf'; sessionId: SessionId }
    | { type: 'split'; direction: 'vertical' | 'horizontal'; 
        ratio: number; a: TileNode; b: TileNode }
  ```
  - Binary splits only (no arbitrary N-way splits)
  - `a` = left/top side, `b` = right/bottom side
  - `ratio` = fraction of space given to `a` (clamped 0.1–0.9)
  - Vertical split = side-by-side (divider runs top-to-bottom)
  - Horizontal split = stacked (divider runs left-to-right)

- **Lines 44-49**: Tab structure:
  ```
  type Tab = {
    id: TabId
    title: string
    root: TileNode        // The tile tree for this tab
    focusedSessionId: SessionId  // Which pane has focus in this tab
  }
  ```

- **Lines 255-301**: WorkspaceState (the root workspace model):
  - `tabs: Tab[]` - array of tabs, each with its own tile tree
  - `activeTabId` - which tab is currently visible
  - `sessions: Record<SessionId, SessionMeta>` - metadata for all live sessions
  - `detachedSessions` - sessions not in any tile tree (Dispatch Mode only)
  - `buried` - hidden-but-live sessions removed from layout
  - `dispatchMode: DispatchModeState | null` - Dispatch Mode state (mutually exclusive with grid)
  - `pinnedSessionIds` - ordered pinned agents in Dispatch

**Persistence Type** (`/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/persistence.ts`, lines 21-53):
- PersistedWorkspace serializes to `~/.config/agent-code/workspace.json`
- Includes entire TileNode tree, SessionMeta, DetachedSessionRecord, all focus ids
- Does NOT persist live runtime state (respawned on load)

**Store Architecture**:
- **Lines 62-88** of `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/hook/index.ts` show zustand slices:
  - `state` = WorkspaceState (zustand slice)
  - `setState` = updater function (identity-stable)
  - `runtimes` = SessionRuntime lookup (per-session feed entries, runtime state)
  - `spotlight` = Dispatch Mode selection state (separate from grid focus)
  - `tileTabs` = TileTabsState (described below)
  - `readerMode` = Reader view state
  - All setters come from zustand and are identity-stable across renders

**WorkspaceHookContext** (`/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/hook/context.ts`, lines 38-117):
- Bundles setters, refs, and helpers into a single stable context object
- All setters are identity-stable (zustand factories)
- All refs are useRef outputs (identity never changes)
- Critical for useCallback dependencies across sub-hooks

---

### (b) RENDERING COMPONENTS (SPLITS / LEAVES / RESIZERS)

**TileTree Recursive Renderer** (`/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/tile-tree/TileTree.tsx`, lines 24-76):
```tsx
function TileTree({
  tabId, node, focusedSessionId, workspace, 
  showStatusMode?, showWorktreeBadges?
}): JSX.Element
```
- Renders a TileNode recursively
- **Leaf rendering** (lines 32-40): calls `renderWorkspaceLeaf` which dispatches to provider-specific TileLeaf component
  - For 'claude' or 'codex': uses provider's custom TileLeaf
  - For 'terminal': uses TerminalLeaf (xterm.js)
- **Split rendering** (lines 43-75): wraps children in SplitContainer with resizer

**SplitContainer** (lines 141-232):
- Flex layout with draggable divider
- Direction determines CSS: `flex-row` (vertical split) or `flex-col` (horizontal split)
- **Sizing** (lines 161-162): 
  ```
  aFlex = { flexBasis: `${ratio * 100}%` }
  bFlex = { flexBasis: `${(1 - ratio) * 100}%` }
  ```
- **Drag handler** (lines 167-211):
  - Document-level listeners capture divider drags
  - `requestAnimationFrame` throttles updates
  - Epsilon comparison (0.001) prevents trivial re-renders
  - On mouse move, calculates new ratio from divider position
  - Calls `workspace.setSplitRatioInTab(tabId, aSessionId, bSessionId, nextRatio)`
- Divider styling: `w-[3px]` (vertical) or `h-[3px]` (horizontal)
- Role: `separator` with aria-orientation

**TileLeaf** (`/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/tile-tree/TileLeaf.tsx`, lines 77-100+):
- A complete "mini Agent Code" pane containing:
  - **PaneHeader** (lines 13-14, imported): project dir, status, close button
  - **Feed** (line 5, imported): structured JSONL transcript display + streaming preview
  - **ComposerInput** (line 17, imported): text input for this pane's session
  - **SlashCommandPicker** overlay: when `/` is typed
  - **Trust dialog** overlay: scoped to this pane
  - **QueueStrip** (line 14, imported): queued messages
  - **ScrollIndicator** (line 16, imported)
  - **PaneToast** (line 15, imported): toast notifications in pane context
- **Focused state** (line 81, 96): receives `focused: boolean` prop
  - When focused, input ref is auto-focused
  - Pane gets visual highlight (border color change via CSS class)
- **Runtime** (line 79): provides SessionRuntime object (feed entries, state)
- **onFocusRequest callback** (line 85): called when user clicks pane or types/pastes
- **All per-session state** comes through `runtime` prop (never direct store access except sendInput to PTY)

**TerminalLeaf** (`/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/tile-tree/TerminalLeaf.tsx`):
- xterm.js instance for shell-only panes
- Sends PTY bytes to xterm, forwards keystrokes to main process
- Standalone (no feed, no composer, minimal header)

**Geometry-aware Navigation** (`/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/tile-tree/geometry.ts`, lines 129-197):
- `findDirectionalNeighbor(root, focusedSessionId, direction)` → SessionId | null
- Builds leaf geometry rects (lines 44-85) and scores candidates by:
  1. Primary-axis gap (smallest = physically adjacent)
  2. Cross-axis overlap (largest = best column/row alignment)
  3. Cross-axis center distance (fallback for asymmetric layouts)
- Reason: tree traversal was always landing on leftmost/topmost leaf, breaking 2×3 grid navigation

---

### (c) AGENT VIEW MOUNTING IN PANE

**Provider-based rendering** (`/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/tile-tree/TileTree.tsx`, lines 103-116):
```tsx
